metadata.name: Idaho Airport Project Prioritization Model
metadata.agency: Idaho Transportation Department (ITD), Division of Aeronautics
metadata.source_citation: ACRP Synthesis 123 (2023), Chapter 4 — State of Idaho case example, pp. 31-33. Sourced from interview with Jennifer Schildgen, Airport Planning and Development Manager, Idaho Transportation Department, April 28, 2022, and ITD General Procedures Manual (internal, not published). Project-purpose points and airport-component points reproduced from Figure 4.2 of ACRP Synthesis 123.

decisions_log.author: APH m49 Sprint 6 reference encoder
decisions_log.decision: Encoded Idaho as 7-criterion multiplicative model with two unusual factors (Project Purpose and Airport Component) modeled as select_one tiers.
decisions_log.rationale: ACRP Syn 123 documents Idaho's distinctive 'why' (Project Purpose, 5-10 pts) and 'where' (Airport Component, 2-10 pts) factors as select_one with ranked tiers — not separate per-purpose 1-10 scales. PCI scoring shown as 'reverse PCI' under review by ITD/Aeronautics Board.

decisions_log.author: APH m49 Sprint 6 reference encoder
decisions_log.decision: Encoded remaining 5 factors with conservative placeholder values from adjacent-state practice; flagged in disclaimer.
decisions_log.rationale: ACRP Syn 123 lists Idaho as having 7 evaluation factors total but only publishes Figure 4.2 (Project Purpose) and a description of Airport Component scoring. The remaining 5 factors are placeholder-encoded with conservative point values derived from common practice. Idaho adoption should reset these to ITD-published values when ITD's revised public implementation manual is released.

criteria.label: Project Purpose
criteria.description: Ranks 'why' a project is being done. Only one purpose is selected, with points ranked against each other. Safety is highest at 10, capacity is lowest at 5.

subcategories.label: Safety
subcategories.condition: Improvements to Runway Safety and Approach Zones, correcting FAA Part 77 surface area penetrations, visual approach aids, RW/TW signs.

subcategories.label: Rehabilitation
subcategories.condition: Pavement rehab where PCI > 50 runways, > 45 taxiways, > 40 aprons. Preserves pavement and extends useful life.

subcategories.label: Planning
subcategories.condition: Master plans, ALPs, NEPA, special studies. Elevated to higher priority by ITD.

subcategories.label: Reconstruction
subcategories.condition: Pavement reconstruction where PCI is at or below rehab thresholds. Rebuilds failed pavements.

subcategories.label: Security
subcategories.condition: Physical security: keeping animals from runway, protecting aircraft from pilferage or malicious damage.

subcategories.label: Maintenance
subcategories.condition: Routine maintenance work that does not qualify as rehab or reconstruction.

subcategories.label: Capacity
subcategories.condition: Projects that increase airport usage: longer runways, more ramp space, parallel taxiways. New or expanded facilities.

subcategories.label: Airport Enhancement
subcategories.condition: Other airport enhancement projects not covered by higher-scoring purposes.

criteria.label: Airport Component
criteria.description: Ranks 'where' on the airport the project is located. Only one component is selected, with existing runway highest at 10 and new airport lowest at 2.

subcategories.label: Existing Runway
subcategories.condition: Project located on existing runway pavement, edge, lighting, or RSA.

subcategories.label: Existing Taxiway
subcategories.condition: Project on existing taxiway or taxilane.

subcategories.label: Existing Apron
subcategories.condition: Project on existing apron pavement, drainage, or marking.

subcategories.label: Landside or Other Existing
subcategories.condition: Landside facilities, hangars, terminal, ops/admin areas, or other existing infrastructure.

subcategories.label: New Airport / Greenfield
subcategories.condition: Greenfield airport development. Lowest component score.

criteria.label: PCI Factor
criteria.description: Pavement Condition Index factor. Idaho currently uses a reverse-PCI scoring (higher PCI awards more points). ITD is revising this in their next manual; this encoding preserves the current direction.

criteria.label: Federal Funding Leverage
criteria.description: Recognizes projects that leverage federal AIP, BIL, or discretionary federal funding to match state contributions.

criteria.label: Idaho Airport System Plan Alignment
criteria.description: Project advances or maintains a goal or recommendation of the Idaho Airport System Plan (IASP).

subcategories.label: Consistent with current Master Plan / ALP

criteria.label: Project Readiness
criteria.description: Whether the project is ready to proceed (CIP-programmed). Placeholder encoding pending ITD published manual.

criteria.label: Airport Classification
criteria.description: Recognizes airport role per IASP classification tiers.

governance.scoring_authority: ITD Division of Aeronautics, Airport Planning and Development Manager
governance.approval_process: ITD Aeronautics enters projects in an internal Excel spreadsheet with drop-down menus for each evaluation factor; spreadsheet auto-calculates priority totals. Manager reviews and presents recommendations to the Aeronautics Board for approval.

disclaimer: SYNTHETIC ENCODING based on publicly available material in ACRP Synthesis 123. Idaho's General Procedures Manual is internal; only two factors (Project Purpose and Airport Component) are published in detail. The remaining factors are placeholder-encoded using common practice from adjacent states. Use only as a benchmarking reference until ITD publishes its revised implementation manual.
